name: Lemon juice whitening

lead: Lemon juice whitening means putting lemon juice, sometimes with baking soda, on the teeth to remove stains and look brighter. It is shared as a natural bleaching method.

Proponents say citric acid bleaches or dissolves stains. Lemon juice is about 5 to 6% citric acid, more than lime and several times more than orange juice. No clinical trials were found, and acids are also the mechanism of dental erosion.

paras: People apply juice with a cotton swab or mix it with baking soda into a paste, leave it briefly and rinse. It is used occasionally as a quick home treatment before events. Users describe the effect as a short-term brightening.
Erosion is irreversible and may expose dentin, causing sensitivity. Dental sources note that exposure frequency matters.

angle.text: Users apply lemon juice, alone or with baking soda, as a natural bleach for stained teeth, crediting its citric acid. It is a quick kitchen routine for a brighter-looking smile. No trials were found, and dental sources associate citrus with enamel erosion.

lead: Lemon juice whitening is a home practice of applying lemon juice, alone or mixed with baking soda, to the teeth to remove stains. It is shared as a natural bleaching method.

Lemon juice is about 5 to 6% citric acid, with more than lime and several times more than orange juice [1]. Dental sources associate acidic foods and drinks, including citrus, with dental erosion [2]. No clinical trials of lemon juice as a tooth whitener were found.

paras: Proponents say the acid and the fruit's reputation as a natural bleach lighten tooth colour. Lemon juice is described in general sources as being used to lighten hair in sunlight [1], and some extend the idea to teeth. The encyclopedic lemon article does not mention teeth [1].
No studies found. Whitening trials in humans have tested peroxide products [3].

Dental erosion is irreversible loss of tooth structure by non-bacterial acids. Citrus fruit and fruit juices are discussed among dietary causes, with frequency of exposure and swishing acidic liquids increasing risk [2]. When enamel is lost and dentin is exposed, dentin hypersensitivity can result, and dental guidance includes limiting acidic foods and waiting before brushing [4].
Lemon juice and baking soda is a recurring item in natural whitening roundups. No community-sourced material was available for citation here.
